thread:
Maya: quick sync — I'm drafting the H2 dedicated capacity roadmap. Need a decision on hybrid burst semantics for customers who use both reserved pools + on-demand. Two open levers: 1) carryover unused burst credits (soft carry) 2) preemptible 'spot' pool reclaim policy. Want to pick a sensible default + gated opt-in.
Arjun: high-level sounds reasonable. Tech constraints: KV cache + continuous batching complicate preemption; preempting active sessions can violate L7 SLOs. We can implement reclaim at slot-level with a drain window.
Sienna: from oncall POV, drain window must be >= 30s for safe quiesce; otherwise we see errors during spike reclaims. Also need observability: per-tenant evictions metric + an alert.
Leo: FYI a major fintech pilot asked for guaranteed short bursts (3x baseline for up to 5m) and an explicit audit trail for evictions. They'll only sign if we promise no preemption during business hours.
Priya: sales note — customers expect clear billing for burst vs reserved. Need deterministic mapping: 'reserved consumed first, burst charged at lower rate, preemptible reclaimed without notice only for opportunistic customers'.
Maya: my proposed default policy: carryover up to 20% of monthly burst credits for 48h; preempt policy: prioritized by 'opportunistic' label, drain=45s, eviction events logged. Launch criteria: docs, canary with 2 internal tenants, metrics surfaced in console (evictions, avg drain time, cost delta).
Arjun: quick proto config snippet for autoscaler routing: 
```
policy: hybrid-burst
carryover_percent: 20
carryover_ttl_hours: 48
preemptible_label: opportunistic
drain_seconds: 45
fallback_model_variant: small-latency
```
Arjun: note — we need to verify kernel-level memory reclaim with the runtime; worst-case might push drain to 60s. Also add a safety throttle to avoid cascading preemptions.
Sienna: monitoring list: tenant.evictions.count, tenant.evictions.rate5m, tenant.drain.latency.p50/p95, tenant.fallback.rate. Proposed SLO: <1 eviction per 1k requests per hour for reserved customers.
Leo: customer asks for a "business-hours exception" flag per contract. Can we support that? How to enforce across regions/timezones?
Maya: technically feasible via tenancy policy + region-aware enforcement, but increases complexity. Proposal: support it on contract + manual opt-in at launch for up to 2 pilot customers, then productize later.
Priya: sounds good — sales will only push if we have pilot docs and the audit log. What's the timeline?
Maya: timeline draft: week 0-2 design + RFC; week 3-6 implement autoscaler + telemetry; week 7-9 canary + pilot; week 10 beta launch. Owners: Arjun (runtime/autoscaler), Sienna (telemetry+alerts), Leo (pilot coordination), Priya (customer comms). PM: Maya.
rfc-bot: RFC posted: https://redwood.infra/rfc/hybrid-burst-2026 — pls review, comments due EOD Fri :eyes:
Sienna: small nit — add rollback policy: automatic fallback to 'fallback_model_variant' + create a ticket if eviction_rate > threshold.
Maya: noted. I'll update RFC with rollout gating and rollback. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Priya: putting this on next sales sync. I'll prep a one-pager for pilots.
Leo: will start outreach to the fintech pilot. tagging @Maya for contract clause details.
Maya: appreciated. Sync tomorrow 10am PT. End.
